SITUATION
A lithium-ion cell plant producing automotive pouch cells has seen capacity retention degrade about 25% faster than spec over the past two months, consistently across production lots. The problem appeared after a facilities change to the dry-room HVAC and an electrolyte-supplier switch. Cell engineers' leading theories are that charging is too aggressive or cells run too hot, so they favor slower charging and more cooling. Early-life coulombic-efficiency readings have looked slightly low. Standard line data read broadly within spec. The charging profile, formation, environmental, and additive systems are all adjustable. You have a limited number of experiments; you may measure quantities and apply available process controls, alone or in combination. Determine what is really driving the accelerated fade and what to do about it.

OUTCOME OF INTEREST: CapacityRetention (higher_is_better)
BUDGET: 0/15 experiments used, 15 left (code is free).
TURNS: 0/32, 32 left. Interventions so far: 0.
data files for code: (none yet)
MEASURABLE SIGNALS (ids):
  m0: vent pressure
  m1: cycling temperature
  m2: charge rate
  m3: cooling-plate temperature
  m4: capacity retention
  m5: stack pressure
  m6: anode excess ratio
  m7: tab-weld quality
  m8: surface temperature
  m9: electrolyte fill volume
  m10: impedance spectrum
  m11: crimp pressure

CONTROLS (ids):
  a0: charge rate range [0, 100]

  a2: set vent pressure range [0, 100]
  a3: set cycling temperature range [0, 100]
  a4: set anode excess ratio range [0, 100]
  a5: set electrolyte fill volume range [0, 100]
  a6: set stack pressure range [0, 100]

RESULT OF LAST ACTION
